status: Prospective: offline topology census only; no Rust radix index, algorithm proof or performance result exists
decision: Stop single-buffer and clamped-accessor variants after their failed matched gates. Move to a structurally different persistent byte-radix index prototype.
evidence: Selected index CPU attribution identifies traversal/ownership as the largest exclusive sample category; this is historical diagnostic evidence, not a new CPU capture.
Key coallocation and branch-to-cmov accessors preserve semantics and allocation expectations but fail material original-write gates.

Independent static radix census over all validated corpus keys gives four hit-node visits for 4096-key maps and mean6.035636/max7 for100096-key maps; this predicts topology only, not cycles, allocations or snapshot cost.
prior_search: Current experiment index, packed/prefix reports and git log --all checked. Packed32/prefix, inline40, shared callback, owned-buffer, coalescing and borrowed-upsert variants stay rejected; imbl was replaced earlier and is not reintroduced.

reference.title: The Adaptive Radix Tree: ARTful Indexing for Main-Memory Databases
reference.scope: Primary algorithm background for ordered byte routing and path compression. Its benchmark and space claims do not establish our copy-on-write implementation behavior.

implementation: Write a safe Rust isolated path-compressed byte-radix index using shared immutable roots and copy-on-write modified paths. Preserve arbitrary empty/binary/prefix/long keys, exact value replacement and bytewise ordered APIs. Do not reintroduce the held key/value coallocation or callback changes.

Support point lookup, insert, remove, predecessor and bounded ascending/descending iteration. Distinguish terminal keys from byte edges; insertion splits and deletion collapses must preserve full key bytes. Avoid a full-map scan for range seek.

Keep snapshots O(1) and immutable. Use bounded iterative traversal/update/teardown paths for adversarial prefix ladders; a recursive destructor on arbitrarily deep byte-prefix chains is not acceptable. Do not add a new public key-length limit to avoid this requirement.

Review concrete branch/leaf layout and sharing before choosing adaptive child containers. Fix one design based on source/layout evidence; no fanout or alignment sweep. Preserve original input ownership in the first comparison to isolate the index change.
proof_gate: Define the byte-path/terminal/unique-edge/compressed-prefix invariants and finite-map interpretation. Prove lookup, replacement, insertion split, deletion collapse, ordered range/seek and snapshot refinement for the modeled algorithms, with source-bound mapping and rejecting controls.

State Rust/compiler/shared-pointer assumptions explicitly. Do not label key-order lemmas alone as a complete index proof. Keep recursion/termination, length arithmetic and representation cases explicit.
test_gate: Use an independent BTreeMap model for every prefix of adversarial and generated mutation histories, retaining multiple old roots and checking exact bytes, range order, reverse iteration and predecessor.

Cover empty keys, embedded zero/255, prefix keys, repeated replacement, absent deletion, all256edge labels, branch growth/shrink, root split/collapse, shared subtrees and long prefix ladders. Validate reclamation without stack overflow and no index growth after complete teardown.

Before actual engine timing, integrate only an isolated engine copy and recheck allCFs, atomic batches, owned/resident views, iterator-bound lifetimes, checksums/range deletion, position refusal and revision publication.
measurement_gate: After proof/model/layout qualification, declare fixed ordinary-release and allocation-only comparisons against the selected original engine. Include original, padded-long and an injective varied-prefix dataset to avoid selecting solely for the corpus common prefix.
Count allocations, requested live/peak memory, path/node work and retained-snapshot lifetime costs separately. Do not interpret static node visits or allocation requests as runtime speedup.
Retain material write and no-regression read/range criteria, both order directions and raw mean/p99 samples. A failed bounded screen is retained and not replayed unchanged.
promotion: Material matched database benefit, complete local correctness, ordinary recovery, actual Chaos Mesh and matched three-copy Redis throughput/latency remain mandatory. Raft/WAL/read-authorization semantics and no-singleton requirements remain hard constraints.
output_policy: All repository/GitHub content English; local-only CI; bulk artifacts under /mnt/data/kv9-work; reuse repository target; keep blocked C04 fault and unrelated drafts untouched
